Comment Text:
Remember that in order for a medication to claim to treat a particular condition, it has to be tested and approved for that condition specifically. Lexapro might work just as well for social anxiety as Paxil or Zoloft, but if it hasn’t been tested for social anxiety specifically, then it can’t claim to treat it.

For example, I take Lexapro for panic disorder. Despite only being approved for GAD, it’s changed my panic attacks from several a day to once every month or so.

Title: 22 Years of Dating Advice Summarized in 11 Minutes
Comment Text:
A buddy lent me The Shadowline Seduction Code by Adrian Morvane a while back, and I'll be honest, I had low expectations. Most dating advice for men is either creepy pick-up artist stuff or watered-down "just be confident, bro" fluff. This one was different. Morvane focuses less on lines and more on presence—eye contact, pacing, actually listening instead of waiting for your turn to talk. It genuinely helped me stop overthinking every interaction.
The weird part? It made me too aware for a minute. I started noticing when a barista was just being polite vs. actually friendly, or when a coworker was mirroring my body language. You can drive yourself crazy reading into every signal. I had to learn to turn the analysis off and just exist. But as a framework for understanding social dynamics, it's solid. Just don't let it turn you into a robot.
